title: Chicken Sorba

ingredients.title: For the Soup
items: Fresh coriander leaves – ½ cup, chopped

ingredients.title: For Garnish & Serving
items: Crusty bread or steamed rice – optional, for serving

instruction.title: Prepare the Broth Base
steps: Heat oil or ghee in a heavy-bottomed pot over medium heat.
Add cumin seeds and whole black peppercorns and let them splutter for a few seconds.
Add the sliced onion and sauté until golden brown.
Add minced garlic, ginger, and slit green chili.
Cook for about 2 minutes until fragrant.

instruction.title: Cook the Chicken
steps: Add the bone-in chicken pieces to the pot.
Sear on all sides until the chicken turns white and develops a light golden color.
Add turmeric powder, red chili powder if using, and salt.
Stir well to coat the chicken with the spices.
Add the chopped tomatoes and cook until they soften and the oil begins to separate.

instruction.title: Simmer the Soup
steps: Pour in 6 cups of water and bring the soup to a boil.
Reduce the heat to low and simmer gently, uncovered, for about 40 minutes.
Cook until the chicken is completely cooked through and tender.
Skim off any foam or impurities that rise to the surface during simmering.

instruction.title: Shred & Finish
steps: Remove the cooked chicken pieces from the broth.
Allow them to cool enough to handle, then remove the meat from the bones and shred it.
Return the shredded chicken to the broth.
Add chopped fresh coriander and lemon juice.
Taste and adjust the salt and black pepper as needed.

instruction.title: Serve
steps: Ladle the hot chicken sorba into serving bowls.
Garnish with fresh coriander leaves and lemon wedges.
Serve hot with crusty bread or steamed rice.

chefTips: Chicken: Bone-in chicken adds more depth and body to the broth than boneless pieces.
Spices: Lightly roast the cumin seeds and peppercorns before adding them to the oil for a deeper aroma.
Aromatics: Add a small cinnamon stick or a few cloves while simmering for an extra layer of fragrance.
Broth: Skim the surface during simmering to keep the sorba cleaner and more refined.
Balance: Add lemon juice at the end so its fresh acidity remains bright.
Serving: Chicken sorba is best served piping hot with fresh coriander and lemon wedges.
